title: The place
subtitle: Hills between Florence and the sea

steps.title: Hills and coast
steps.body: Tuscany, in central Italy, stretches from the Apennines in the east to the Tyrrhenian Sea in the west. Most vineyards are on hills between 150 and 600 m, among olive groves and cypresses. The heart is Chianti, between Florence and Siena. South are Montalcino and Montepulciano; on the coast, Bolgheri and the Maremma.

steps.title: Mediterranean with altitude
steps.body: Tuscany has a Mediterranean climate: hot, dry summers and mild winters. Inland, altitude and hills bring cool nights that preserve acidity. The coast is warmer, with sea breezes. Soils include galestro, a crumbly schist-like marl, and alberese, a hard limestone, both prized for Sangiovese.

steps.prompt: Which soils are prized for Sangiovese in Tuscany?
steps.explanation: Galestro marl and alberese limestone give fine Sangiovese.

steps.title: History
steps.body: The Etruscans made wine here before the Romans. In 1716, Cosimo III de' Medici, Grand Duke of Tuscany, defined the boundaries of Chianti, Carmignano, Pomino and Valdarno, one of the earliest legal wine regions. In the 1870s, Baron Bettino Ricasoli set a Chianti formula led by Sangiovese.

steps.explanation: Yes, by Cosimo III de' Medici.

steps.title: What you learned
points: Tuscany runs from the Apennines to the sea
Hills and altitude cool its Mediterranean climate
